title: SLO meshing workshop — action plan (30/60/120)
content:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the proposed structure and outputs for a cross-functional \"meshing\" workshop to align Service Contracts, Behavioral SLOs, and on-call/runbook practices across product, infra, serving-runtime, and SRE. The goal is a repeatable 30/60/120-day program that yields: a canonical SLO mapping for 6 critical services, a small set of testable canaries, updated runbooks, and a telemetry signal catalog with concrete alert/update rules.

Background & motivation:
- We have drift between product-level availability promises (contracts) and the telemetry-derived SLOs teams actually measure. This causes mismatched expectations during incidents and inconsistent rollback thresholds.
- The Meshing workshop is intentionally tactical + hands-on: bring engineers, product managers, on-call leads together for rapid alignment and artifact creation.

Objectives (what success looks like):
1) For 6 prioritized services (see Scope) produce a 1-page SLO contract that ties user impact to specific telemetry measures (error_rate, p50/p95 latency, saturation).
2) Produce a minimal automated canary definition per service that can run in CI and exercise SLO boundaries.
3) Create runbook updates (escalation & mitigation) that reference the SLO contract and show exact rollback/mitigation thresholds.
4) Define ownership for SLI collection and a short-term instrumentation patch list.

Scope (explicit):
- In-scope: API gateway, text-generation-serving, inference-queue, embeddings-service, routing-layer, billing-sync (6 services).
- Out-of-scope: long-tail infra services, third-party partner endpoints.

Who should attend (roles):
- Product owner for each service (maps user contract to impact)
- Service engineering lead (implementation, rollout)
- Observability engineer (dashboards, SLI collection)
- SRE on-call rep (runbook & incident ops)
- Solutions/SE rep where customer SLAs are impacted

Workshop format (day-by-day snapshot):
- Prework (week prior): collect existing SLO docs, SLAs, and current dashboards. Observability team provides a raw signal dump for each service.
- Day 1 (Alignment): 3hr cross-team session to review user-impact scenarios and pick primary SLI/metrics. 2hr breakout per service to draft the 1-page SLO contract.
- Day 2 (Instrumentation & Canary): 2hr session to design automated canaries; 2hr engineer pairing to stub SLI exporters or queries.
- Day 3 (Runbooks & Escalation): 1.5hr review of typical incidents and define mitigation paths tied to SLO thresholds; finalize runbook templates.
- Async follow-up week: observability team implements data collection changes; engineering teams submit PRs for canaries.

Key outputs (artifact list):
- 1-page SLO contract (title, owner, user-impact, SLI definition, SLO target, error budget policy) per service
- SLI query snippets and dashboard snapshots (Grafana/Prometheus)
- CI canary job definition (Jenkins/GHA snippet)
- Runbook update PR template and at least two updated runbooks per service
- Short instrumentation backlog (3–6 items) with owners and target dates

30/60/120-day program (milestones & cadence):
- Day 0–30 (Sprint 1): run workshop, lock contracts for 6 services, land basic SLI queries and dashboard panels, merge canary stubs to feature branches.
- Day 31–60 (Sprint 2): complete instrumentation fixes, enable canaries in CI experimental lane, begin running canaries nightly, collect initial canary results and adjust thresholds.
- Day 61–120 (Sprint 3): promote canaries to canary lane for rolling deploys, formalize error-budget cadence in team rituals, complete runbook rollouts and on-call training sessions.

Roles & RACI (brief):
- Product Owner: R (responsible for contract wording)
- Service Eng Lead: A (accountable for implementation, owner of PRs)
- Observability Eng: R (SLI collection + dashboard)
- SRE Oncall Lead: C (consulted for runbooks and escalation)
- Program Lead (Aisha Patel): I (coordinates schedule, workshop facilitation)

Measurement & acceptance criteria:
- Each service has a published SLO contract in Confluence with sign-off by Product Owner and SRE on-call lead.
- SLIs are queryable in our metrics backend and dashboarded (panel visible) for each service.
- At least 4/6 services have a successful nightly canary run by day 60; 6/6 by day 120.
- Runbooks updated and referenced by the SLO contract; at least one tabletop per service completed by day 120.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps are larger than estimated. Mitigation: reduce service count to 4 for initial run and expand in next program wave.
- Risk: Cross-team scheduling slips. Mitigation: reserve calendar blocks, use async templates for prework and a 1-pager stub approach to keep momentum.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from new SLI-derived alerts. Mitigation: gate alerts behind error-budget policies and use composite alerts for material impact only.

Communication plan:
- Weekly short status notes in #reliability-workshop channel (2–3 bullets).
- Fortnightly show-and-tell demo to platform stakeholders.
- Confluence page updated after each workshop day with outputs and action items.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed (workshop kickoff agenda items):
- Confirm whether billing-sync is considered customer-facing for contractual purposes. (Owner: Priya)
- Decide standard SLO window (30d vs 7d-peek + 30d rolling). (Owner: Miguel)
- Determine whether canaries run against prod-mirrors or a synthetic test harness. (Owner: Service Eng Leads)

Immediate next steps (before first workshop):
1) Program lead (Aisha) to schedule three half-day blocks and send attendee prework checklist (due 5 business days before).
2) Observability to export raw metrics and a sample dashboard for each service (JIRA-REL-2145).
3) Product owners to bring user-impact scenarios (2 per service).
4) Create Confluence workspace and template pages (linked_artifacts above).

Appendix (scratch notes / templates):
- 1-page SLO contract template (scratch):
  - service: 
  - owner: 
  - user-visible impact description: 
  - SLI(s): query + measurement window + cardinality notes
  - SLO target and rolling window:
  - error budget burn policy: what triggers rollback / mitigation
  - runbook link: 

- Canary skeleton example (GHA YAML snippet):
  name: canary-smoke
  on: schedule
  jobs:
    smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
      - run: curl -f https://canary.example.internal/health?sim=smoke
      - run: run-canary-checks --expected-p50=120 --expected-error-rate=0.02

Notes to self (workshop facilitator style):
- Keep the workshop output-oriented. Encourage teams to produce a mergeable PR for at least one SLI query by EOD.
- Defer philosophical SLO debates (e.g., exact window choice) to a decision log and move forward with a pragmatic default.
